child_hunger.summary: No new Hagerty-specific statements on child hunger, SNAP, or food insecurity were found in the July 7–13, 2026 window. However, major Tennessee SNAP developments continued to unfold. A July 10 Tennessee Lookout investigation published widely confirmed that approximately 100,000 Tennesseans have lost SNAP benefits since the One Big Beautiful Bill Act took effect in July 2025, with total recipients falling from 696,000 to 597,890 — one in seven who relied on the benefit no longer receiving it. Advocates noted barriers have made it harder for 'working families, older adults, veterans, and children' to access nutrition assistance. A July 8 WKRN report on the law's one-year anniversary showed Tennessee Democrats warning of worsening hunger impacts, while Sen. Marsha Blackburn (not Hagerty) defended the law. The federal court ruling voiding Tennessee's Healthy SNAP junk-food restriction waiver — confirmed by a July 10 Shelby Report article — remained in effect. No new Hagerty statements on these topics were found in the July 7–13, 2026 window.
child_hunger.details: Three major Tennessee SNAP stories published July 7–13 are relevant context: (1) The Tennessee Lookout investigation (widely republished July 10) documented 100,000 Tennesseans losing SNAP since July 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, with the Tennessee Justice Center stating new barriers 'have made it harder for working families, older adults, veterans, and children to access the nutrition assistance that they are qualified to receive.' Tennessee adopted broad-based categorical eligibility in June 2026, raising the income limit to 200% FPL and eliminating the asset test — but enrollment remains well below pre-law levels. (2) A July 8 WKRN report marked the One Big Beautiful Bill's one-year anniversary, noting the Tennessee Democratic Party claims 104,000 Tennesseans lost health coverage and nearly 100,000 lost SNAP; Sen. Blackburn defended the law but Hagerty's office did not respond. (3) A July 10 Shelby Report confirmed the Healthy SNAP Tennessee waiver (which would have restricted junk-food purchases) was permanently halted after a June 22 federal court ruling, with TDHS instructing retailers to remove all related signage. Hagerty made no public comment on any of these developments during the window.
